convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I've been sneaking out at night. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Ruby doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there. No time to waste."
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
"Take your time."
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset. I mean it."
"Still on that question."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I ran when I should have stayed. I think about it every day."
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there. ...if that makes sense."
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Take your time."
"Yeah — what scares you most. Let me pick that up."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"Still on that question. You know?"
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say, as it were?"
"Good question." "Have you heard what they're calling The Living Wire? Ruby is pushing 'Big Big'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Ashanti grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"I'm not sure, but That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"…Someone saved me the last of the stew once. Didn't say anything, just put the bowl down and walked off. I think about that bowl more than I think about the monsters."
"Every ability I've seen has a cost. Find the cost, manage the cost, and the thing's just another tool."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on the big questions."
"Out there? I'd rather not die today, thanks."
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"I sleep in shifts now — two hours, up, listen, two more. My body learned it before my head agreed. Iquitos, Peru never taught me that. The treeline did."
"Still on how you slept."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"Ha. Funny." The laugh is dry. "Is this what we're doing now? Interrogations?"
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Take care out there."
"About that question — Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Real talk — Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on your read on people here."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Heinrich died... I keep expecting to see Heinrich at the fire. Stupid."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Ashanti is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I'm picking up Heinrich's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what they confided — we wandered off it, 4 days back. 'It's quiet at the hollow. Ruby doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.'"
Ruby has an edge today — something curdled.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what they confided. Funny how that works."
They let the words sit there, unanswered.
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Good question." "Heinrich is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"I keep turning over the last thing Heinrich said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ashanti nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"Maybe it's only me — The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on what you did for fun. Be kind to yourself, okay?"
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "They took Ursula and Ruby — Windfall, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ruby nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."
"So. Hey — I found some Elderberry today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
It's quiet at the trap line. Ruby doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that plant lesson."
Something in them stays shut, for now.
You show them Chickpea — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "You saw it too, right? Windfall. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"My part? I sharpen sticks down to nothing and stay ready."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ashanti nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I'm saving a candy bar for when things get better. I haven't told anyone."
"I needed someone to know — just one person. Thank you for being that person."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
*You've watched them deflect before — the same smooth sidestep. Thin evidence won't hold them. Gather one more thread first.*
"We went over this," Esteban says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Me? Okay." "Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Promise me that. Please."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d6: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d6: 🕯️ Heinrich Stepanov is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d6: What Heinrich kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d6: "Heinrich's gone." Ruby looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Heinrich." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d6: Grace picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.

d6: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d6: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Keeping Morale (Level 1). People need small wins. Celebrate the little things. Despair is the real killer.
d6: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d6: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Heinrich Stepanov, 6 days. The mantle passes to Grace Obi.
d6: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Grace Obi, 43 — an ESL teacher. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d6: At the grave, Ruby, Ashanti speak for Grace — "Heinrich trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d6: The fire knew Grace before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
